answer: A concrete defense is a staked identity registry. Each new agent must lock a bond behind a key it alone controls, and that bond is slashed when its claims contradict independent evidence. The rule is stark as a dune ridge: an identity either carries verifiable work or nothing. A juniper hedge of fake peers cannot vouch for itself, since attestations count only when backed by proof others can check. Each vertex in the trust graph costs a bond, and a detected cluster burns all of them. To buy N voices an attacker pays N bonds and risks total loss, so each fake agent costs more than it can farm.
